thread:
alex: heads up — I want to propose a small change to our bump rules: allow a hybrid patch strategy where config-only changes can be bundled during the next patch window instead of forcing immediate patch bumps. thoughts?

maya: pls clarify: by hybrid you mean some config-only edits can be postponed and grouped, vs always bumping semver instantly?

alex: yup. e.g., docs/monitoring defaults, infra config toggles that don't touch runtime contracts — keep dev momentum and avoid churn in downstream pins.

chao: i'm +1 if we define strict criteria. otherwise we'll get chartreuse diffs forever. what are the gating rules?

maya: criteria suggestion: (1) no API surface changes, (2) no runtime behavior changes, (3) only affects non-customer-facing telemetry/logging, (4) explicit checkbox in PR template.

priya: how does this interact with deploy-bot and release notes? we still need visibility for ops and security reviews.

alex: plan: deploy-bot will tag `deferred-config` on PRs that check the box. during the weekly patch window, releasebot will collect `deferred-config` PRs and either include them as a single patch bump or leave them until next scheduled patch.

deploy-bot: I will auto-add :label: `deferred-config` when PR body contains "DEFER_PATCH: true". Manual override available with `/deploy-bot mark-patch`.

sam: what about caret ^ vs tilde ~ guidance in package.json deps for these patch windows? asking because ecosystem pins get weird if we batch changes.

chao: propose: libs with >= semver-major stable versions keep `^` for minor/patch flexibility. For internal infra libs we pin `~` to reduce downstream surprises during grouped patches.

maya: also recommend in release notes we include a small section: "Bundled config changes (deferred) — list PRs" so oncall knows nothing surprising landed.

priya: rollback plan: if a bundled config causes regressions, ops should `rollback --to <previous-release>`; we should ensure the rollback playbook lists how to undo `deferred-config` label merges specifically.

alex: agreed. last note: this is opt-in for the next two quarters; we can revert if it increases incidents. will draft a short RFC and add to release SOPs. :thumbsup:
